headline: This fall needs immediate attention
whatWeNoticed: What you've described includes one or more signs that can indicate a serious injury or medical emergency after a fall.
whatDeservesAttentionFirst: Safety comes first. If your parent lost consciousness, can't be woken easily, has a severe or worsening headache, has vomited repeatedly, had a seizure, or has sudden weakness or trouble speaking or seeing — call 911 now.
helpfulObservationsToMonitor: Whether they are alert, responsive, and stable right now
Any bleeding, visible injury, or inability to move a limb normally
Whether confusion or drowsiness is getting better or worse
todayThisWeek: If there is any doubt about safety — call 911 or go to the emergency room now.
For a possible fracture, inability to get up, or new confusion without other severe symptoms, seek urgent medical care today.
Do not wait to 'see if it gets better' when any of these signs are present.
commonMistakesToAvoid: Waiting to see if symptoms improve on their own.
Assuming a fall was minor because your parent seems okay right after it — some symptoms (confusion, bleeding on the brain) can appear later.
Moving someone who may have a fracture or head/neck injury before help arrives, unless they're in immediate danger.

withYourParent: Stay calm and reassuring — your steadiness helps them stay calm too.
Explain simply that you're getting help to keep them safe.
withFamily: Alert family immediately so someone can be present or on call.
Decide quickly who is going with them or meeting them at care.

questionsForHealthcareTeam: Given these symptoms, should we go to the ER now or is urgent care appropriate?
What follow-up or monitoring is needed after today?
What new symptoms should prompt us to seek help again right away?
whatMayBeComingNext: Getting prompt care now is what gives the best outcome after a serious fall.
Once the immediate concern is addressed, a falls-risk evaluation can help prevent this from happening again.
howToPrepare: Have their medication list and key medical information ready to bring or share.
Keep emergency numbers and their doctor's contact information easy to find.
whatThisDoesNotMean: Needing urgent care now does not mean every future decision has to be made today.
It does not mean your parent has lost their independence.
suggestedNextSteps: Afterward, book a consultation to plan next steps and falls prevention.
